overview.text: The Army plans to detonate five tons of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday, and residents are bracing for a possible lead dust plume.
The Justice Department apologized for making a false statement to a judge in the Ilhan Omar search case.
Kilmar Abrego Garcia is leaving the U.S. for Spain, ending a 20-month legal fight after his wrongful deportation.
Republican Dan Sullivan conceded the Alaska Senate race to Mary Peltola.
A federal jury found Huawei guilty of stealing U.S. trade secrets but acquitted it of racketeering.
Wisconsin reported its third measles death a day after Pennsylvania's ninth, bringing the U.S. tally to 14.

stories.headline: ✅ Spurs 123, Kings 107
stories.summary: Final · at Kings · Record 15-3

stories.headline: BermudAir adds nonstop San Antonio flights to Belize City and Grand Cayman
stories.summary: Two seasonal nonstop Caribbean routes were announced out of San Antonio International Airport. The airport waived landing and departure fees to land the new service.
stories.why: New nonstop options expand vacation travel from San Antonio.

stories.headline: San Antonio airport says it has staff for Thanksgiving rush
stories.summary: San Antonio International Airport says it has enough staff for the Thanksgiving crowds as hiring continues. Travel is already picking up at the airport.
stories.why: Helps travelers plan for a busy holiday week.

stories.headline: Mayor says ICE arrest at West Side site had no city link
stories.summary: San Antonio's mayor said an ICE arrest at a West Side waste collection site involved no city association.
stories.why: Shows how federal immigration enforcement is touching local city operations.

stories.headline: Army to detonate five tons of lead azide in Iowa
stories.summary: The Army plans to detonate 68 barrels of lead azide at an Iowa ammunition plant Wednesday morning after delays. Residents were warned to stay indoors amid conflicting information on how far toxic lead dust could travel.
stories.why: Affects the health and safety of residents in the plume's path.

stories.headline: Alaska ends voter data sharing with Justice Department
stories.summary: Alaska's Republican elections chief ended an agreement that gave the Justice Department the state's detailed voter list and let it flag voters for removal.
stories.why: Touches on voter privacy and federal searches for noncitizen voters.

stories.headline: Student who lost eye at 'No Kings' protest sues government
stories.summary: Tucker Collins, 19, says a federal agent shot him in the eye with a projectile while he documented a Los Angeles protest. He is suing the federal government.
stories.why: Raises questions about federal agents' use of force at protests.

stories.headline: Justice Department apologizes for false statement to judge in Omar case
stories.summary: The department acknowledged making a false statement to a judge hours after the House's top lawyer said it mischaracterized his view on constitutional protections for lawmakers.
stories.why: Bears on limits of federal searches of sitting members of Congress.

stories.headline: Sullivan concedes Alaska Senate race to Peltola
stories.summary: The Republican conceded five days after the Trump administration gave up on a long-shot lawsuit meant to potentially block certification of the race.
stories.why: Settles a Senate seat and affects the chamber's balance.

stories.headline: Trump awards Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom
stories.summary: Trump presented the honor to Giuliani, a longtime ally whose reputation was tarnished by his efforts to overturn the 2020 election on Trump's behalf.
stories.why: A notable use of the nation's highest civilian honor.

stories.headline: Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. for Spain, ending legal fight
stories.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, wrongly deported last year, is voluntarily leaving for Spain. He had faced the prospect of deportation to Liberia.
stories.why: Closes a high-profile immigration case lasting 20 months.

stories.headline: Iranian singer and four crew receive 74 lashes each
stories.summary: Parastoo Ahmadi and four production team members were flogged after being sentenced for offending public decency by publishing content online. Western governments and rights groups call flogging torture.
stories.why: Shows Iran's continued harsh enforcement of dress and content rules.

stories.headline: Leaked data: over 300 Russians killed propping up Mali's junta
stories.summary: Leaked records list 349 deaths in three years among Russian fighters in Mali. They also shed light on Russia's military activity elsewhere in Africa.
stories.why: Reveals the scale of Russia's military role in Africa.

stories.headline: Huawei found guilty of stealing U.S. trade secrets
stories.summary: A New York federal jury found Huawei guilty of stealing source code and technology from companies including T-Mobile and Cisco, but acquitted it of racketeering.
stories.why: A major ruling in the U.S.-China technology fight.

stories.headline: Investigators find Nvidia chips illegally diverted to China
stories.summary: Justice Department investigators have gathered evidence of Nvidia chips being illegally diverted by other firms to China, while Attorney General Blanche downplayed questions about Nvidia.
stories.why: Ties into export controls and the ongoing Nvidia controversy.

stories.headline: Treasury's financial crimes bureau discloses cybersecurity incident
stories.summary: FinCEN said unauthorized access affected a limited subset of its systems. It has not disclosed the full scope or source.
stories.why: The bureau holds sensitive financial intelligence data.

stories.headline: Medicare hospice caps leave some patients without care
stories.summary: Critics say payment limits to hospice companies penalize patients who are not dying on the government's timetable.
stories.why: Affects care for seriously ill Medicare patients and their families.

stories.headline: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
stories.summary: Doctors say disinformation is driving refusals of routine newborn vitamin K shots, which prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.
stories.why: A preventable risk to newborns.

stories.headline: This group of seamstresses mends shirts to make chemo easier for cancer patients
stories.summary: Seamstresses in Ohio and other states are making zippered shirts for cancer patients so they can more comfortably undergo chemotherapy treatments.

stories.headline: U.S. preparing new tariffs on major trading partners
stories.summary: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.
stories.why: Tariffs can raise prices for consumers.

stories.headline: UK households face soaring gas bills under new price cap
stories.summary: Regulator Ofgem's new price cap will raise domestic gas prices significantly in January.
stories.why: Signals higher household costs in Britain this winter.

stories.headline: ‘Carthage Resident Al Gore’ Buys His Hometown Tennessee Newspaper
stories.summary: Former vice-president, who started his career as a journalist, purchases Carthage Courier in Smith county Al Gore, who started his career as a journalist, is returning to the industry as a newspaper owner in his Tennessee town.

stories.headline: Boise State drops out of College Football Playoff rankings
stories.summary: After a chaotic Week 12, Boise State fell from 17th to unranked after a last-second loss. No Group of 6 team is in the rankings, though Boise remains in the projected field.

stories.headline: CFP committee moves Tennessee ahead of Alabama
stories.summary: The committee vaulted Tennessee past Alabama in the rankings. Committee chair Hunter Yurachek said it was not due to public pressure.

stories.headline: 'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt
stories.summary: Manchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt, as displayed in their laborious Champions League draw against Napoli.

stories.headline: Smithsonian head defends autonomy after report of Trump overhaul plan
stories.summary: Lonnie Bunch wrote to staff after an outline of major personnel and programming changes was seen on a White House aide's computer.
stories.why: Concerns the independence of the nation's museums.

stories.headline: How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region
stories.summary: Washington's $9 billion industry grows more than 70% of the nation's fresh apples. Farmers are being pressed by high costs, tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.

stories.headline: Substance released at concert could be linked to robberies, police say
stories.summary: Police are investigating a possible link between the Co-op Live evacuation and reported robberies.

today.summary: Cloudy today, with a high of 56° and a low of 43°. No rain expected.
